name: Ethics and Responsibility II
description:
Sustainability and biodiversity are now widely discussed narratives in the public sphere. However, moving beyond these narratives and focusing on concrete implementation activities reveals the significant challenges involved. Current public debates about wolf and bear populations in Europe vividly illustrate the conflict between ecological demands and human interests.
How can these conflicts be resolved? An interdisciplinary dialogue between the natural and social sciences and ethics is essential to ensure that not only do both sides benefit from their respective demands, but, more importantly, that solutions can be implemented more effectively. Developing models for the more successful implementation of such solutions will be the goal of this project seminar.
prerequisites: Die Studierenden sollten über Grundkenntnisse im Bereich der Angewandten Ethik verfügen.
